name: The Boo Radleys
label: Creation Records
lede: A band from Wallasey named after a recluse in a novel went from shoegaze to Giant Steps, then to a No. 1 album led by a song Martin Carr wrote after a night on acid.

eras.title: Named after a man who never leaves the house
eras.text: Three friends from Wallasey, across the Mersey from Liverpool, took their name from Boo Radley in Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird. Martin Carr wrote the songs and rarely sang them; that was Sice's job.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · Wikipedia: Martin Carr
years.h: Sice, Carr and Tim Brown start a band in Wallasey
years.p: Simon 'Sice' Rowbottom sings, Carr plays guitar, Tim Brown plays bass, and [[Steve Hewitt|5976af3a-ab6a-4725-a9cc-72cdffc6b932]] drums. One early gig is at the Grand nightclub in New Brighton.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Ichabod and I comes out on tiny Action Records
years.p: The debut sells little, but it gets the attention of Rough Trade Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Everything's Alright Forever · Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: After a BBC session, Rob Cieka takes over the drums
years.p: Hewitt goes on to drum for [[Placebo|847e8284-8582-4b0e-9c26-b042a4f49e57]], until 2007.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · Wikipedia: Everything's Alright Forever
years.h: Three EPs on Rough Trade, then Rough Trade goes under
years.p: The Every Heaven EP is out shortly before the label collapses in 1991. [[Alan McGee|ffacc13a-01e5-4b5d-a455-6a7f302ac9ce]]'s Creation Records signs them right after, and the Adrenaline EP follows.

eras.title: Pedals out, trumpets in
eras.text: The press filed them with the shoegazers, and for one album it fit. Then 'Lazarus' arrived, and Giant Steps, named after the John Coltrane record, brought in trumpet, cello, clarinet and dub.

years.src: Wikipedia: Everything's Alright Forever · Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: The Creation debut is cut at First Protocol in London
years.p: Recorded in autumn 1991, it reaches No. 55. A US tour supporting [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]]'s [[Sugar|e3347fbd-2595-480e-926d-278566debf9d]] follows.

years.src: Wikipedia: Everything's Alright Forever · Sic Magazine: The Boo Radleys
years.h: 'Does This Hurt?' leads the Boo! Forever EP
years.p: Sic Magazine later called it arguably their best song before Giant Steps.

years.src: Sic Magazine: The Boo Radleys · Wikipedia: Giant Steps
years.h: 'Lazarus' trades the effects pedals for 1960s psychedelia
years.p: The single stalls at No. 76. Sic Magazine, comparing it with 'Does This Hurt?', called the change a quantum leap.

years.src: Wikipedia: Giant Steps · Sic Magazine: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Giant Steps: Coltrane's title, the Boos' own record
years.p: Sixty-four minutes recorded in February and March at First Protocol, with trumpet, cello and clarinet in the mix. It reaches No. 17 and, at 60,000 copies, is Creation's best seller of 1993.
years.xp:
The band produced it themselves with engineer Andy Wilkinson. Pitchfork later heard "a grand vision that unifies psychedelia, British guitar-pop, jazz, and dub."

Sic Magazine compared the jump to Radiohead going "straight from Pablo Honey to OK Computer."

years.cap: Ticket for the Limelight, New York, November 16, 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: A La's cover for So I Married an Axe Murderer
years.p: The band records The La's' 'There She Goes' for the Mike Myers comedy's soundtrack.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · Wikipedia: Giant Steps
years.h: In the NME's year-end poll, only Björk beats them
years.p: The NME's verdict, 9 out of 10. Giant Steps finishes second to [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]]'s Debut with the critics, tops the readers' poll, and is Select's album of the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wake Up!
years.h: To Rockfield in Wales to make Wake Up!
years.p: Two months at the Monmouthshire studio, produced by the band with Wilkinson engineering.

eras.title: A No. 1, then a left turn
eras.text: Britpop was peaking, and Creation's John Andrews put real marketing behind the band. Carr wanted nothing to do with the scene, and the follow-up went somewhere else entirely.

years.cap: On the cover of Melody Maker, February 18, 1995
years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · Wikipedia: Wake Up!
years.h: Carr writes 'Wake Up Boo!' watching The Big Breakfast after acid
years.p: Their only Top 10 single peaks at No. 9 and stays on the chart for two months.

years.cap: Sice, Carr, Brown and Cieka, c. 1995
years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · Wikipedia: Wake Up!
yt: 'Wake Up Boo!' on Top of the Pops, 1995
years.h: Wake Up! goes to No. 1
years.p: The fourth album tops the UK chart. 'Find the Answer Within' (No. 37), 'It's Lulu' (No. 25) and 'From the Bench at Belvidere' (No. 24) follow.
years.xp:
Carr, in 2005: "I tried to have nothing to do with what was being called Britpop... I didn't like most of the new bands or the flag-waving."

The album page credits Creation's John Andrews with the marketing push, which the band initially resisted.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: 'Oh Brother' goes on Help for War Child
years.p: The Boos share the charity album, for children in Bosnia, with [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] and [[Manic Street Preachers|32efea44-6cb5-4b4f-bdaa-c8b8f6cef981]].

years.src: Wikipedia: C'mon Kids
years.h: C'mon Kids: louder, stranger, No. 20
years.p: Recorded at Rockfield again. The title track, at No. 18, is their last Top 20 single, and the NME gives it 9 out of 10.
years.xp:
The band tells two versions. Sice, in 2005: "We wanted to take them with us to somewhere that we'd not been before." Carr has said the album was meant to alienate the new fans.

Writer David Cavanagh's tally: the band "lost 100,000 fans" and went back to being a cult act.

eras.title: Kingsize and a phone call
eras.text: The last album peaked at No. 62. A few months later, Carr called time.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Kingsize reaches No. 62
years.p: One single, 'Free Huey!', makes No. 54. The title track is lined up as the next single when the band stops.

q: It was such a relief when Martin phoned me
years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · 3:AM Magazine: Leave Them All Behind
years.h: Martin Carr phones Sice to say he's done
years.p: Sice, in a 2006 interview: he'd barely had the heart to go to the studio during Kingsize. The Boo Radleys end after about a decade.

eras.title: Bravecaptain, Paperlung, and a request from Afghanistan
eras.text: Carr made records as Bravecaptain, the name lifted from a fIREHOSE song. Sice stepped away from music for years, then came back with a new band.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Find the Way Out collects the Creation years
years.p: A compilation; The Best of the Boo Radleys follows in 2007.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · 3:AM Magazine: Leave Them All Behind
years.h: Sice returns with Paperlung and an album, Balance
years.p: Singles 'The Days That God Sold You' and 'Do What Thou Will' come first. Before that he sang on two tracks for Japanese musician Ryo Matsui's project Meister.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Forces radio opens its Afghanistan studio with 'Wake Up Boo!'
years.p: BFBS picks the song after it tops a listeners' poll.

eras.title: Three Boos, no Carr
eras.text: Twenty-five years after Wake Up!, Sice, Brown and Cieka started recording again. Carr wasn't asked, and has said so.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Tim Brown, from Top of the Pops to teaching IT
years.p: A BBC profile finds the bassist teaching at St Louis Grammar in Kilkeel, County Down, after building a studio and training as a teacher at John Moores University.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys · Wikipedia: Martin Carr
yt: 'A Full Syringe and Memories of You'
years.h: 'A Full Syringe and Memories of You', 23 years on
years.p: The first new Boo Radleys music since Kingsize comes out as an EP, without Martin Carr, who says he wasn't consulted.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Keep On with Falling, the first album without Carr
years.p: Sice, Brown and Cieka's first full album together since Kingsize, 24 years earlier.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: Eight, plus a Giant Steps reissue and a tour
years.p: Announced in January with the single 'Seeker', alongside a reissue of the 1993 album and UK and Ireland dates.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: 'Lazarus' closes Shinichiro Watanabe's new anime, Lazarus
years.p: The Cowboy Bebop director uses the 1992 single as the ending theme.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boo Radleys
years.h: In Spite of Everything makes nine albums
years.p: The third record of the reunion era.
